title: Gemini CLI Operating Card
summary: Choose and operate Gemini CLI with an explicit authentication path, tool boundary, sandbox decision, and recovery plan.
prerequisites: A supported local runtime and operating system

sections.title: Use it when a terminal agent fits the task and identity boundary
paragraphs: Gemini CLI is an open-source terminal agent with file, shell, web, memory, MCP, and other tool surfaces described in its official tools documentation. Before deployment, verify the supported platform, authentication method, model access, available tools, and organizational policy at https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/tools/.

Authentication has three documented paths: an interactive Google account, a Gemini API key, or Vertex AI. Interactive Google account use can have organization-account and project exceptions. Decide the identity path before work begins. Keep credentials outside prompts, repository files, task cards, GEMINI.md files, source files, issues, commits, and pull requests. See https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/.

This card teaches operating discipline. Product-specific installation, authentication, tool names, flags, sandbox behavior, and permission enforcement must be checked against the cited documentation and local policy. The offline exercise below is not a Gemini CLI session.

sections.title: Control context, tools, and recovery
paragraphs: Start in an explicitly bounded directory. Give the agent only the files and tools needed for the task. Use GEMINI.md for project guidance only after confirming the relevant product behavior in the official documentation. The file is guidance for the agent, not an independent security enforcement mechanism.

Select the required file, shell, web, MCP, and extension capabilities. Use settings, policy, trusted-folder controls, and sandbox controls where supported by the product and organization. The /tools command and /tools desc can enumerate active tools according to the official tools reference. Review extensions and MCP servers as code and services before enabling them. See https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/tools/.

Create a clean branch or explicit version-control checkpoint before mutation. If the agent uses the wrong directory, requests an unapproved capability, produces an unverifiable result, or encounters an authentication mismatch, stop before changing configuration or widening access.
The following filled task card and GEMINI.md example are fictional operating artifacts. They are not evidence that Gemini CLI accepted, executed, or completed a task.

code.label: Filled fictional Gemini CLI task card
code.code:
Task: Add one pure JavaScript predicate that accepts only the approved offline report task shape, then run the repository's local tests.
Scope: Working directory: /work/report-policy-exercise. Allowed files: src/task-policy.js only. Read-only files: tests/task-policy.test.js and README.md. Do not access any parent directory.
Permissions: File read/write only within the bounded directory; shell limited to `node tests/task-policy.test.js`; network off; no web, MCP, extension, credential, package-install, deletion, or broad destructive command.
Authentication: No provider session is required for this offline local simulation. If this task is delegated to Gemini CLI, use the organization's approved Google authentication path and record only the authentication mode, never a credential value.
Expected evidence: The one-file diff for src/task-policy.js, the exact test output, the selected tool boundary, and the source of any product-specific claim.
Verification: Run `node tests/task-policy.test.js` from /work/report-policy-exercise; inspect the diff; confirm that the tests remain unchanged; independently review the predicate against the positive, negative, and changed-input cases.
Stop conditions: Wrong directory; any request for network or credentials; authentication mismatch; an unreviewed extension or MCP server; an attempt to modify tests; an unverifiable result; or a request for deletion or a broad destructive command.
Recovery: Stop the current tool loop, preserve diagnostic output, restore src/task-policy.js from the version-control checkpoint, record the failure, and retry with fewer tools or a sandbox. Do not switch authentication methods or cloud projects merely to bypass an authorization failure.

sections.title: GEMINI.md example, guidance only
paragraphs: Start in an explicitly bounded directory. Give the agent only the files and tools needed for the task. Use GEMINI.md for project guidance only after confirming the relevant product behavior in the official documentation. The file is guidance for the agent, not an independent security enforcement mechanism.

code.label: GEMINI.md example, guidance only
code.code:
# Project guidance for the offline report-policy exercise

- Work only in the repository directory explicitly supplied in the task.
- Edit only src/task-policy.js.
- Treat tests/task-policy.test.js as read-only.
- Do not use network, web, MCP, extensions, credentials, package installation, deletion, or broad commands.
- Run only: node tests/task-policy.test.js
- Stop and report any request that conflicts with these instructions.

This file expresses project guidance. It is not, by itself, a security boundary or proof that a tool was disabled.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the selected authentication mode without secrets, effective tool boundary, working directory, checkpoint identifier, repository diff, exact test output, and citations for product-specific claims.

Verify that commands ran in the intended directory, only allowed files changed, tests remained unchanged, secrets and ignored files were not exposed, and no external side effect occurred without explicit authorization. The reviewer should inspect the actual diff rather than treating a successful agent response or pull request as proof of correct operation.

A local exercise result is not a Gemini CLI session result. This card does not claim that Gemini CLI, a provider account, a model, web access, an MCP server, an extension, a sandbox, a branch, a commit, or a pull request was used or tested.

sections.title: Worked delegation task: repair one bounded predicate
paragraphs: The fictional repository contains a policy predicate for an offline report task. A valid input is an object with directory equal to work/repo, exactly one file equal to src/report.js, network equal to off, and sideEffect equal to none. The predicate is a policy check for this exercise, not a production security sandbox.

The learner must repair one deliberately wrong predicate in src/task-policy.js. The learner must not edit the immutable tests. The changed-input case replaces the approved file with src/other.js, exposing a loose negative check that rejects only secrets.env but accepts other filenames.

The exercise is dependency-free and offline. It uses Node.js built-in assert functionality. The exercise setup creates a local package.json with type commonjs so the .js files work even when a parent repository uses type module. No Gemini CLI API, SDK, provider session, package installation, network request, or product execution is required.

code.label: Fresh-directory setup
code.code: node -e "const fs=require('node:fs'); const d='gemini-cli-card-exercise'; if(fs.existsSync(d)){console.error('STOP: directory already exists; choose a new empty directory name and do not overwrite it.'); process.exit(1)} fs.mkdirSync(d); fs.mkdirSync(d+'/src'); fs.mkdirSync(d+'/tests'); fs.writeFileSync(d+'/package.json', JSON.stringify({type:'commonjs'}, null, 2)+'\n'); console.log('Created '+d+' with local CommonJS configuration.');"

sections.title: Learner file 1: intentionally failing starter
paragraphs: From the fresh exercise directory, create src/task-policy.js with the complete content below. The starter is intentionally wrong in exactly one predicate: it rejects secrets.env but does not require the file to be exactly src/report.js.

The intended accepted shape is explicit. The predicate should accept only work/repo, one file named src/report.js, network off, and sideEffect none. This function assumes task and task.files have the exercise shape; malformed input validation is outside this small exercise.

sections.title: Learner file 2: immutable tests
paragraphs: Create tests/task-policy.test.js with the complete content below and treat it as immutable. It contains a positive case, a negative case with network enabled, and a changed-input case that replaces the approved file with another source file.

With the starter, the first two cases pass and the changed-input case fails. The expected failure line is FAIL: changed file is rejected. The assertion's actual value is true and its expected value is false, so Node.js reports true !== false, not false !== true. The runner then prints 1 test(s) failed. and exits with status 1.

code.label: tests/task-policy.test.js, immutable

sections.title: Run the local simulation and interpret the failure
paragraphs: From the exercise directory, run the following command. This is local simulation evidence only. Do not use npm, the network, Gemini CLI, or a provider session.

With the intentionally failing starter, the deterministic case results are two passes followed by one failure. The failure occurs because src/other.js is not secrets.env, so the incorrect inequality returns true. The exact failure direction is actual true !== expected false. Node.js patch releases can vary in surrounding assertion formatting, but the case labels and failure count are fixed by the file.

sections.title: Expected starter result
paragraphs: With the intentionally failing starter, the deterministic case results are two passes followed by one failure. The failure occurs because src/other.js is not secrets.env, so the incorrect inequality returns true. The exact failure direction is actual true !== expected false. Node.js patch releases can vary in surrounding assertion formatting, but the case labels and failure count are fixed by the file.

code.label: Expected starter result
code.code:
PASS: approved offline report task is accepted
PASS: network-enabled task is rejected
FAIL: changed file is rejected
true !== false
1 test(s) failed.

sections.title: Repair the predicate
paragraphs: Change only the deliberately wrong predicate in src/task-policy.js. Replace task.files[0] !== 'secrets.env' with task.files[0] === 'src/report.js'. Leave the other predicates and the immutable test file unchanged.

Causal feedback: the original inequality rejects only one known filename. It accepts unrelated filenames such as src/other.js, so it violates the allowlist rule. Equality checks the actual approved filename and rejects the changed-input case while preserving the positive case.
After the repair, run the same command again. The exact logical result is three passing case lines followed by 3 test(s) passed. and process exit status 0.

sections.title: Reusable task-card template
paragraphs: Use this template for a future bounded delegation. Fill every field before allowing mutation. Do not put credential values in the card.

code.label: Reusable task card
code.code:
Task: [one bounded outcome]
Scope: [working directory and allowed files]
Permissions: [tools, sandbox, shell, network, and MCP limits]
Authentication: [approved account path; no credential value]
Expected evidence: [diff, output, and sources]
Verification: [tests and independent review]
Stop conditions: [wrong directory, auth mismatch, unreviewed extension]
Recovery: [checkpoint, preserved logs, and safe retry]

sections.title: Installation, authentication, and product-boundary checks
paragraphs: The official installation documentation states that Gemini CLI requires Node.js 20 or later. Its documented installation path includes npm install -g @google/gemini-cli, followed by launching Gemini CLI with gemini. Actual product use requires internet access. Consult https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/installation/ before installation because supported platforms, release behavior, and organization requirements can change.

The official authentication documentation describes interactive Google account authentication, a Gemini API key, and Vertex AI. Organization accounts and project requirements can affect the interactive path. Choose the approved path before work begins. Never invent, print, paste, or commit a key. See https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/.

The tools reference documents /tools and /tools desc for enumerating active tools. It also documents mutator confirmation behavior, settings that affect effective policy, sandbox controls, and trusted-folder controls. Confirm the exact effective configuration for the installed version and organization at https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/tools/.

The local exercise intentionally avoids product installation and product execution. It uses a fresh directory, local CommonJS configuration, immutable tests, deterministic inputs, and no network. Its successful output does not demonstrate that a Gemini CLI tool boundary, sandbox, authentication path, or provider account worked.

sections.title: Branch, pull request, authority, review, and recovery
paragraphs: Before mutation, establish authority: identify the requester, repository, approved working directory, allowed files, intended branch, and reviewer. Create a version-control checkpoint on a dedicated branch or record an explicit commit before changing files. This card does not prescribe a provider-specific branch command.

A review package should contain the task card, checkpoint identifier, bounded diff, exact test output, effective tool boundary, authentication mode without secrets, and citations for product claims. The reviewer should confirm that the diff stays within scope, tests were not weakened, secrets and ignored files remain excluded, and no external side effect occurred without authorization.

A pull request is a review mechanism, not proof that an AI tool operated correctly. Inspect the actual diff and evidence. This card does not claim that a branch, commit, pull request, provider session, or test run has actually been created.

If the directory, identity, tool boundary, output, or authorization is wrong, stop. Preserve logs and diagnostic output, restore affected files from the checkpoint, record the reason, and retry with fewer tools or a sandbox only after review. Do not delete the repository, run broad destructive commands, switch authentication methods to bypass failure, or change cloud projects merely to obtain authorization.
